reason: Waiting for Bridge or Photoshop to launch just to look at one file is the thing I hate most, and a viewer that opens in about 120-350 ms and steps at 40-50 ms is exactly what I'd set as the double-click default. It's free and per-user, so trying it costs me nothing.
why_switch_or_not: I'd make it the default for double-clicking files in Explorer and for a quick look at RAW and JPG, because of the speed numbers and because RAW and JPG show as separate pictures, which is how I cull. I would NOT move my catalogue or Lightroom/Bridge ratings and keywords over. Nothing in the description says it reads or writes XMP, star ratings or colour labels, so it stays next to Adobe, not instead of it.
current_app_pros: Bridge and Lightroom hold my catalogue, ratings, labels, keywords and XMP sidecars, and the colour management matches what I deliver. Photoshop opens anything and edits it. Nothing else has my 15 years of metadata.
current_app_pains: Slow to open. Bridge and Photoshop take seconds to launch just to look at a file, and flipping through RAWs in Bridge lags while it builds previews. Heavy on RAM and subscription-priced.
objection: My colour management, catalogue and XMP workflow must not change. I can't see any mention of XMP or ratings, and a developer-measured benchmark on one PC with a version 0.4.1 from a single person isn't proof it stays fast on my 200,000 pictures or that it won't mangle my sidecars.
would_change_my_mind: Proof it reads and honours XMP ratings and labels without writing anything to my files or sidecars unless I ask, and that it stays this fast on a folder of thousands of RAWs on my own machine.
